# P2.4 text-editing fixtures (the §6 gate matrix)

These PDFs are the **gate** for P2.4 Stage 1 (constrained in-place text editing). They
are deliberately tiny, committed, and generated by `src-tauri/src/editor/testpdf.rs`
through lopdf's **public API only** — the same library the product writes with — so a
fixture that lopdf cannot express is a real signal about what Stage 1 can express.

Regenerate with:

```bash
scripts/make-p24-fixtures.sh
```

Only re-run when a builder in `testpdf.rs` changes; the committed bytes are what the
tests read.

## Which gate each fixture exercises

| Fixture | Gate (P2.4 §3) | What it must provoke |
|---------|----------------|----------------------|
| `simple-winansi.pdf` | happy path | `/Type1 /Helvetica /WinAnsiEncoding`, three pages, two runs each. Editable. |
| `simple-embedded-subset.pdf` | (c) not subset | `ABCDEF+` prefix on `/BaseFont` → `TEXT_RUN_NOT_EDITABLE`, gate `not-subset`. |
| `cid-identity.pdf` | (a) simple font | `/Type0` + `/Identity-H` → `TEXT_RUN_NOT_EDITABLE`, gate `simple-font`. |
| `roundtrip-fail.pdf` | (b) encoding round-trip | `/Differences` with two names mapping to U+0020, so a byte decodes to a space and re-encodes to a *different* byte → gate `encoding-round-trip`. |
| `too-wide.pdf` | (d) width | One very short run (`HI`), so a plausible replacement overflows the advance width → `TEXT_RUN_NOT_EDITABLE`, gate `fits-width`, quoting both measured widths. The gate is evaluated at edit time from PDFium-measured widths; the fixture only has to provide a genuinely narrow run. |
| `encrypted-aes.pdf` | T7 / T8 | AES-128, user password `secret`. Opens read-only; every edit refuses `ENCRYPTED_READ_ONLY`; "Decrypt a copy" produces `{stem} (unprotected).pdf`. |
| `multi-stream-page.pdf` | F2 collapse | `/Contents` is an array of two streams. lopdf concatenates them, so runs from both are located and the edited page collapses to one stream (legal; D2 copy semantics leave the original's layout alone). |
| `reflow-line.pdf` | P2.8 §6.2, row A10 | Line 1 is one `TJ` array — `ALPHA `, a `-120` kern, `BETA` — behind a **single** `Td`, so moving its tail must *insert* a positioning operator; line 2 (`WXYZ`) is placed by its own `Tm` and must not move. Ends 389 pt clear of the 612 pt box. |
| `reflow-line-near-edge.pdf` | P2.8 §6.2, R3 refusal | The same two lines starting at x=452, so line 1 ends **9.064 pt** from the box — less than one replacement's worth of room, which is what `fits-width` needs in order to refuse. |
| `bomb.pdf` | (e) / F3 cap | A 16 MiB stream that compresses to a few KB, beyond the 8 MiB `CONTENT_LIMIT` → `CONTENT_TOO_LARGE`. |

## Honest limitations

Two gates cannot be produced as a *committed file* that also behaves as the gate
requires, because a PDF that genuinely exhibits the failure would need a font program
this repo does not ship. Both are covered by in-memory unit tests in
`src/editor/textedit.rs` and `src/editor/testlocate.rs`, which build the same shape with
lopdf and assert the refusal — so **no gate is untested**:

* **Gate (b), round-trip failure.** The committed `roundtrip-fail.pdf` carries the
  `/Differences` collision, and lopdf's own `get_font_encoding`/`string_to_bytes` decides
  the verdict at runtime. That is the honest, non-hand-crafted version of the fixture:
  the gate fires because lopdf's inverse map really does lose one of the two names. The
  unit test `refuses_an_unroundtrippable_encoding_with_gate_b` asserts it directly.
* **Gate (c), subset font.** The `ABCDEF+` prefix is real subset-naming evidence and is
  all the gate inspects (Stage 1 does not open the embedded program — T11). The committed
  fixture therefore *does* provoke the refusal; the note here is only that it is a name
  convention we match rather than a program we parse.

`sample.pdf` predates this matrix and remains the best-case regression fixture for the
earlier phases.
